provenance.note: Three deposited states of Bacillus PS3 ATP synthase from one cryo-EM dataset: 6N2Y (3.0 Å), 6N2Z (3.0 Å) and 6N30 (3.2 Å) (Guo, Suzuki and Rubinstein, eLife 2019). Prepared from a rigid-composite recipe: states 2 and 3 are superposed on state 1 using the stator, and each state keeps its own chains (suffix -1, -2, -3): the three beta subunits, gamma, epsilon, the ten c subunits and subunit a. The alpha subunits, delta and the peripheral stalk are left out to fit the headset budget, and side chains are kept only on state 1's subunit a and marked c subunit. Each chapter shows one deposited state; the motion between states was not observed.

chapters.title: State 1 of 3
chapters.caption: Entries 6N2Y, 6N2Z and 6N30 are three deposited states of one enzyme, aligned on its fixed parts. This is state 1: the three beta subunits, the rotor, and subunit a beside the ring. The alpha subunits and the peripheral stalk are left out.

immersive.narration: State one: beta subunits around the rotor, subunit a by the ring.

chapters.title: Three different sites
chapters.caption: One beta subunit is closed on Mg-ADP, one is open with a putative phosphate modelled at its site, and one is held open by epsilon with its site empty. The same three colours mark these conformations in every state. Beta-TP, beta-DP and beta-E name the three positions around the rotor; in this inhibited state epsilon holds the beta-DP site open and empty (Guo et al. 2019).

immersive.narration: Amber: closed on ADP. Blue: putative phosphate. Green: open, empty.

chapters.title: State 2
chapters.caption: In 6N2Z gamma has turned about 120 degrees counterclockwise, seen from the head, the direction of ATP synthesis, and the c-ring about 108 degrees. The closed, putative-phosphate and empty conformations have each moved one beta subunit round with gamma. Each chapter is a deposited state; the motion between them was not observed.

immersive.narration: State two: gamma turned about 120 degrees; each beta site changed.

chapters.title: State 3
chapters.caption: In 6N30 gamma has turned about another 120 degrees. Ten c subunits cannot split into three equal steps: measured against subunit a, the deposited ring positions differ by about 108, 144 and 108 degrees, that is 3, then 4, then 3 c subunits (Guo et al. 2019).

immersive.narration: State three: the ring moved three c subunits, then four.

chapters.title: Back to state 1
chapters.caption: Three more c subunits bring the rotor back to state 1. Ten c subunits make one turn, so ten protons cross the membrane for each full turn of the rotor.

immersive.narration: Back to state one: ten c subunits, ten protons, one full turn.

chapters.title: Where protons cross
chapters.caption: Protons enter from outside the cell through a half-channel in subunit a and bind Glu56 on the ring. After almost a full turn each reaches Arg169 and leaves into the cell. In state 1, Glu56 of the marked subunit is 3.7 Å from Arg169.

immersive.narration: Protons bind Glu56, turn with the ring, and leave at Arg169.

chapters.title: Eleven nanometres apart
chapters.caption: Arg169 is 11 nanometres from the ADP in the closed site. The rotor couples proton flow in the membrane to the catalytic sites in the head.

immersive.narration: Proton exit and closed catalytic site are 11 nanometres apart.
